A_general.open_code_note: No official public repository or package for the hosted server was found in the evidence folder. The hosted endpoint is documented by MailerLite; no public code was available to establish implementation equivalence.
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: Changelog says endpoint moved to the 2.x MCP SDK in v4.14.0; exact SDK version NOT FOUND.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: MailerLite's MCP feature page says “Connect for free” and that it is free to start. No separate MCP charge or MCP-specific usage price was found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: MailerLite lists multiple plans, including a free starting option and paid plans. Exact prices and plan limits were not reliably extracted from the captured pricing page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The MCP page describes free initial access; the linked email marketing service has plan-based pricing. No MCP per-call charge or MCP-specific quota was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth authorization is required. ChatGPT eligibility is documented as Pro and Plus on the web; its developer documentation says web eligibility is available to Pro and Plus accounts. Cursor's free plan may have a 40-active-tools-per-connector limit, a client limitation rather than a MailerLite server limit.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: MailerLite controls server authorization; the user's MailerLite account and the AI client control account access and client-side connector limits.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: 2026-07-28 and earlier revisions listed in the changelog
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted server advertises MailerLite account tools. The official reference groups tools across subscribers, campaigns, groups, segments, fields, forms, automations, templates, email content, e-commerce, webhooks, discovery, and authentication.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool results and errors are not comprehensively specified in the main reference. The changelog documents JSON-RPC errors for unknown tools and argument validation; individual tools may return structured result objects.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official tool list includes list_resources and fetch, which are tools for resource discovery and retrieval. No evidence was found that MCP resources are separately exposed through resources/list.
The documentation provides example prompts for AI clients. It does not establish that the server exposes MCP prompts through prompts/list.
No server logging capability or MCP logging notifications are documented in the reviewed materials.
No MCP sampling support is documented in the reviewed materials.
No MCP roots support is documented in the reviewed materials.

A request to the endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge referencing protected-resource metadata. The metadata identifies the authorization server as https://mcp.mailerlite.com. OAuth metadata advertises authorization code and refresh-token grants, S256 PKCE, dynamic client registration, and client authentication methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none. No scopes_supported or token-lifetime value is advertised in the supplied metadata. Revocation endpoint is the token endpoint.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Bearer token in the Authorization header. Protected-resource metadata lists bearer_methods_supported: ["header"].
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration. Raw metadata: resource=https://mcp.mailerlite.com/mcp; authorization_servers=[https://mcp.mailerlite.com]; authorization_endpoint=https://mcp.mailerlite.com/authorize; token_endpoint=https://mcp.mailerlite.com/token; registration_endpoint=https://mcp.mailerlite.com/register; response_types_supported=[code]; response_modes_supported=[query]; grant_types_supported=[authorization_code, refresh_token]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=[client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none]; code_challenge_methods_supported=[S256]; revocation_endpoint=https://mcp.mailerlite.com/token; client_id_metadata_document_supported=false; scopes_supported not present; token lifetime not present.

No MCP Tasks support is documented in the reviewed materials.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The changelog says unknown tools return JSON-RPC -32602 errors and invalid arguments return validation errors. Search returns warnings for some failed or truncated resource lookups and an error if all lookups fail.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: JSON-RPC error for unknown tools and invalid arguments; search may return a warnings array.

The hosted server uses streamable HTTP. The changelog says clients supporting protocol revision 2026-07-28 are served statelessly without an initialize call or session ID; earlier supported revisions remain listed.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: For the stated stateless protocol mode, no session ID is used.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official list contains read and write operations, including destructive operations such as delete tools. Tool annotations are not published on the reference page. Changelog documents annotation changes for send_test_automation (idempotentHint true to false); complete annotation coverage was not found. 2. No enforced confirmation parameter or server-side approval flow was found. Documentation recommends drafts and user confirmation before sending campaigns; this is a documented behavior promise, not evidence of an enforced approval gate. 3. OAuth authorization is required; scopes_supported, token lifetime, role inheritance, admin switches, redirect approval, and client allowlists are not specified in the supplied metadata or reviewed docs. 4. No server read-only mode, toolset filter, or per-region endpoint was found. Cursor clients may disable selected tools; the free Cursor plan may limit active tools to 40. 5. No MCP-specific field masking or PII exclusions documented. The help article says accessible data can include subscriber names, emails, status, groups, fields, and activity history. Changelog says fetch no longer exposes webhook secrets. 6. Search is documented as searching only the first 50 records of each resource type; its result limit is 1–20, default 10. It can report failed/truncated types in warnings. Other quotas, rate limits, bulk caps, and MCP call costs were not found. 7. Changelog documents invalid-argument errors; details of validation and correction are not specified. Search requires query; fetch requires a search-derived ID or bare ID plus type. 8. MCP-specific audit logging or telemetry disclosures were not found in the reviewed pages. 9. No feedback, rating, report, or survey tool appears in the official tool list. No MCP upsell result was found. 10. The server exposes ordinary tools; no server-delivered skill tool or initialize instructions were found. Docs examples and descriptions guide client behavior but do not establish server enforcement. 11. No persistent agent-memory or behavior-dependent tool availability is documented. 12. Changelog describes a stateless mode for protocol 2026-07-28; no sub-server hierarchy or proxy is documented. E-commerce tools combine multiple actions behind an action parameter. 13. batch_requests is a multi-operation tool; no unrestricted raw API request, SQL, script, or arbitrary execution tool is documented.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Always call search before fetch — fetch requires an id from these results (or a bare id plus an explicit type; see the fetch tool description).
Always call search first to obtain this id — never guess or fabricate one.
A campaign can be built and written for you, but nothing gets sent without your explicit confirmation.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The official reference presents a flat list but the e-commerce area consolidates multiple operations behind action-parameter tools. The changelog also documents protocol-dependent stateless handling. No nested sub-server hierarchy was found.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list is https://developers.mailerlite.com/mcp and names 77 tools. The v4.14.0 official changelog names seven additional tools absent from that page's list; these are included as official with availability marked unknown because the page does not confirm their current default enablement. Two names, forget_subscriber and get_single_import, were added from the Claude connector directory as third-party names absent from the official list. Claude says “Show all 45 tools”; only a subset of names is visible in the captured page, so the remaining names could not be read. Cogny reports 19 tools on its separate proxy endpoint and is not evidence for this endpoint's tool set. No official total is stated. The list file contains 86 entries.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim complete tools/list definitions and initialize instructions were available. The official reference gives names and short summaries but not full input schemas or server instructions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: MailerLite provides product functionality beyond the MCP tool list, including broader email marketing, website/blog, landing page, booking, and other account features. The MCP docs describe only the listed tool surface; exact unavailable human-only operations were not exhaustively enumerated in the reviewed materials.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Examples page says: “These are starting points, not a fixed menu” and prompts may need refinement depending on the client. It labels prompts that change the account as [ACTION]. The docs say to search before fetch and use the result ID; changelog descriptions instruct clients accordingly. Server enforcement is not fully established by these recommendations.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Feature page states: “A campaign can be built and written for you, but nothing gets sent without your explicit confirmation.” It also says users approve access and can disconnect in MailerLite settings. The help article says authorizing gives the chosen AI assistant access to data needed for requests. AI policy and DPA were reviewed; no MCP-specific retention, model-training, or audit terms were identified in the captured relevant excerpts.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: MailerLite describes the MCP server as a secure bridge and says users approve access before connecting. Feature page says campaign drafts are created first and require confirmation before sending.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata supports the documented authentication requirement. The published tool list includes send/scheduling-related and destructive operations, while documentation promises campaign confirmation. No confirmation mechanism or enforcement is documented in tool schemas; treat the confirmation statement as a documentation-level promise rather than verified server-side control.

contradictions: The official reference page's available-tool list omits seven tools explicitly added by the official v4.14.0 changelog: add_automation_step, copy_automation_step, delete_automation_step, reorder_automation_step, replace_automation_trigger, update_automation, and update_automation_trigger.

The Claude connector directory reports 45 tools and visibly lists forget_subscriber and get_single_import, which do not appear in the captured official reference list. Its remaining tools are hidden behind “Show all 45 tools” in the captured copy, so a complete comparison was not possible.

MailerLite's feature page promises campaigns are drafts first and nothing is sent without explicit confirmation, while the official tool list includes schedule_campaign and send_test_automation. The reviewed materials do not show a server-enforced confirmation gate for these operations.
observations_for_research: MailerLite documents tool behavior both through a categorized reference and a versioned changelog; the current page list and changelog additions are not fully synchronized.
Several e-commerce tools multiplex list, get, create, update, delete, import, attach, and detach operations through an action parameter.
The changelog records a transition to stateless handling for the newest protocol revision while retaining support for older revisions.
Campaign confirmation is a prominent product-level assurance, but its relationship to server-side enforcement is not specified in the published tool schemas.
notes: Reviewed the evidence folder's links.json, pages/INDEX.txt, official developer reference, examples, changelog, help, feature, pricing, AI policy, DPA, OAuth metadata, Claude connector listing, Cogny listing, and links_check.txt. No official hosted-server source repository or package was found; the similarly named GitHub link in the evidence check returned 404. No official endpoint-specific install page could be retrieved because it returned HTTP 401. Third-party Cogny and Composio surfaces were not used as evidence for the hosted server's actions. Pricing page was available, but exact current plan prices were not extracted.
